description.narrative:
A new project page to bring together the multiple KRCS projects within the umbrella of Climate Resilience, 2026 onwards. Components will include Food Security and Livelihoods (Taita Taveta, Makueni), Enabling Youth for Climate Action (Y adapt), and Nature Based Solutions (Lamu, Kwale). Communities in Kenya’s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs), including Taita Taveta and Makueni Counties, continue to face increasing climate-related shocks that undermine food security, livelihoods, water access, nutrition outcomes, and household resilience. Recurrent droughts, erratic rainfall, environmental degradation, weak market systems, and limited livelihood diversification continue to disproportionately affect vulnerable households, particularly women, youth, and marginalised groups. In Makueni County, poor rainfall performance, declining crop yields, water scarcity, and high poverty levels continue to drive food insecurity and livelihood vulnerability, while communities in Taita Taveta remain exposed to climate-induced livelihood and agricultural shocks. KRCS, with support from the British Red Cross (BRC), proposes an integrated climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods programme aimed at strengthening adaptive capacity and improving long-term resilience among vulnerable rural communities. The programme adopts a multi-sectoral and community-driven approach integrating climate-smart agriculture, irrigation and water systems strengthening, nutrition-sensitive programming, market systems development, youth innovation, ecosystem restoration, Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA), Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI), safeguarding, and National Society Development (NSD).
Key interventions will include expansion of climate-smart agriculture and irrigation systems, livestock and pasture improvement, strengthening farmer groups and savings structures, rehabilitation of water infrastructure, hygiene and sanitation promotion, community-based nutrition screening and education, and support to youth-led innovation and entrepreneurship initiatives. The programme will also strengthen community governance structures, feedback and complaints mechanisms, and inclusive participation to ensure accountability, sustainability, and equitable access to services. KRCS has developed a strong, evidence-based youth climate action programme through a phased approach, beginning with the Valuing Water Youth Journey and the Y-ADAPT toolkit to build youth knowledge and local adaptation skills. Phase 3 of the Empowering Youth for Climate Action aims to address rising climate risks by strengthening youth capacity in climate awareness, adaptation, livelihoods and advocacy, while promoting inclusive, youth-led climate action systems through localized climate finance, gender and disability inclusion, and greater youth participation in climate governance.
